what: The white 'Your usual week' card starts at y=177 while the band's content runs to about y=190. The card covers the lower half of the sub-line 'Your usual week, used to build your schedule' and the bottom third of the glass 'Change one week' pill. The pill also sits on the 812px column edge (x=919–1108) while the card is 1080px wide (ends x=1376), so the two right edges disagree. Under the card a second white strip with its own shadow carries 'One-off days off go in Requests.', which reads as a card inside a card.
why: Clipped text and a half-covered control (better-layout: never park an action where it clips; better-interface escalation: control overlapped). It is the single most 'unfinished' frame in the set. Shared edges (CR-402) and no card-in-card.
fix: On wide screens give the Availability form the same placement as every other kept form: margin 24px 0 32px (remove '.c-avail--phone' from the :not() list). Move 'Change one week' to the band's right slot at the grid edge (right: 0 of the 1080px grid, 48px tall glass pill). Make the footnote the card's own footer: one white surface, 1px --b-line top rule, 13.5/18 --b-grey, left-aligned at the 22px inset, no second shadow.
where: src/components/employee-b/time.css:147 (margin: -40px lift); src/app/app/employee-b-desktop.css:671 (exclusion keeps the lift on desktop); src/app/app/employee-b-desktop.css:286-290, 538 (centered note)

what: Things to do says 7 and shows three rows on a phone: 'Review swap request' and two 'Review coverage offer'. The two required items ('Confirm this week's schedule', amber 'Action needed', with the teal Review pill) are rows 4 and 5, so they only exist on desktop. On the phone the one thing the manager asked for is not on Home at all.
why: Visual hierarchy and order by importance (better-layout). The phone is the primary device; the required action must be first, and the one teal action on Home disappears.
fix: Order the list required-first before slicing: required items (earliest deadline first), then optional ones by deadline. Phone keeps 3 rows, desktop 5. The first required row keeps the teal 'Review' pill at every width.

what: 'Did I get paid?' is answered with two dates and no state. 'Last pay statement / Fri, Nov 13 / For work Nov 2 – 8' has no status chip and no amount. The only action, 'View statement', is a teal text link with a 32px icon circle, 38px below the text with nothing between. The earlier list shows 'Fri, Nov 6' twice (Corrected, Replaced) as the only other content.
why: The page's one job has no visual answer; the primary action is the weakest element on the card (one primary action per view; a control styled like text does not read as a control). Gusto and Homebase lead this screen with a status and a figure.
fix: Card header: title 'Last pay statement' plus a green chip (b-chip--ok) with a check, text 'Statement ready'. If the page's read already carries net pay, show it as the 30/36 700 tabular figure and move the date to the sub-line ('Paid Fri, Nov 13 · for work Nov 2 – 8'); if it does not, keep the date as the figure (needs Jose: showing an amount is a product and privacy decision, and may need the read to carry it). Replace the link row with a full-width 48px teal pill 'View statement' (phone) and a 48px teal pill hugging its label at the card's foot (desktop). 16px between sub-line and button.

what: Two filled teal pills with the glow on one screen: 'Confirm' and 'See' (open shifts), plus the glass 'Availability'. 'See' is a one-word label that names no object. On the phone the open-shift title wraps to 'pick up' on a second line because the 96px pill takes the room.
why: DESIGN.MD B1: one teal primary per screen. Squint test: two equal teal blobs, the eye cannot pick. Verb-first label with its object (better-writing).
fix: Confirm stays the only teal pill. Open shifts becomes a plain navigating row: title '2 open shifts', sub 'Tue, Nov 17 · tap to pick one up', trailing CaretRight (no button). If a button is kept, make it the ghost kind, 44px, label 'View shifts'. After the week is confirmed the open-shift row may take the teal pill.

what: Every row is a category name: 'Team update', 'Team update', 'Shift request update', 'Time-off update', then five identical 'Schedule update / Action needed' rows. Nothing says which request, which week, or whether it was approved. 'Did my request go through?' needs a tap on each row.
why: Recognition over recall; the list is not scannable and five identical rows look like a bug. Information density is low: 64px rows carrying two words.
fix: Row title = the outcome, sub = the object: 'Time off approved' / 'Nov 30 – Dec 2'; 'Swap request waiting' / 'Wed, Nov 11 with Maria'; 'Schedule changed' / 'Week of Nov 9 · 2 shifts'. Decided items lead with a 36px circle in the state colour (green check approved, grey x declined). The labels come from the server (generic on purpose today), so this needs a contract decision; until then collapse repeats of one kind and week into one row with a count ('Schedule update · 5').

what: Each open shift row ends in its own filled teal 'Pick up' pill with the glow: two primaries stacked 91px apart on the phone.
why: DESIGN.MD B1: 'rows in a list share one kind (ghost), 44px tall, 96px min'. Repeated filled buttons flatten hierarchy and make the list look heavier than the header.
fix: Row buttons use the ghost kind (#F0F2F3 fill, ink 600, 44px, min-width 96px), label 'Pick up'. The teal pill belongs to the confirm step after a row is chosen.

what: Left figure reads '17 h/56 h' with the second number at about half size and no space, then 'hours worked of scheduled', which wraps to two lines on the phone so the left cell holds four lines and the right three. The payday figure is 'Nov 20' on the phone and 'Fri, Nov 20' on desktop, while the Pay page says 'Fri, Nov 20' at both widths.
why: The figure is not readable at a glance and the caption is not a sentence. Two formats for one date (consistency). Uneven cells break the strip's baseline.
fix: Figure '17 h' with small ' of 56 h' (14/600, one space before, --b-on-band-2); caption 'worked this week' on one line (label becomes 'Hours'). Payday: 'Fri, Nov 20' at every width (it fits: 11 characters at 24/700 in a 175px cell), caption 'in 9 days'. Add font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums to .b-live__v.

screens: Home Things to do, 1440 (Employee and Lead)
what: Five rows, three shapes: 64px rows with grey icon circles and a chevron; an 88px row with a teal icon, the amber chip on its own line and a teal 'Review' pill; an 88px row with a teal icon, chip and chevron. In the Lead layout (wider card) the chip sits on the title line and the rows are 65px, so the same card looks different by role.
why: Rows in one list should share height and trailing element (rhythm, CR-004; alignment of trailing edge). Mixed icon tints read as two unrelated lists.
fix: All rows min-height 72px. Chip always on the title line (nowrap; title may ellipsize before the chip wraps). Trailing slot fixed at 96px so the pill and chevrons share one right-aligned column. Every lead icon uses the 36px teal-50 circle with an 18px bold teal glyph (B5 rule); the amber chip alone carries 'required'.

what: Trailing cluster is a time, an 8px teal dot stacked under it, then a chevron. Rows without a dot leave the time centred; rows with a dot push it up 8px, so the right column zigzags. Today rows put the time at the right ('12:47 AM'); Earlier rows put the date at the right and the time in the sub-line ('Action needed · 7:47 PM'), and one row's sub-line is only '8:47 PM'. 'Action needed' is plain grey text here and an amber chip on Home.
why: Inconsistent trailing elements and two places for the same datum; state shown two ways across screens (single voice, TS-006).
fix: One trailing line, vertically centred: [dot 8px] [time], 6px gap, 13/18 --b-grey tabular-nums, right-aligned; Today shows '12:47 AM', Earlier shows 'Nov 9, 7:47 PM'. Sub-line holds only the amber 'Action needed' chip (same b-chip amber as Home) or nothing. Unread rows keep the 600 title; read rows 500.

what: The chip 'For work Nov 9 – 15' and the glass button 'See your hours' sit side by side at different heights: 24px and 32px on the phone, 30px and 42px on desktop. The chip is white with teal text on the phone and dark teal with mint text (#A8F0E4 on #1F403B) on desktop. On desktop 'Pay history' (band) and 'See all' (Earlier card) both open the same page.
why: Two pill sizes on one baseline look accidental; one chip, two colourings; duplicate entry points compete.
fix: Make the period plain band text, not a chip: 'For work Nov 9 – 15' at 14/20 --b-on-band-2 under the date. Keep one glass pill 'See your hours' at 44px (phone) / 48px (desktop). Desktop keeps 'Pay history' in the band and drops 'See all' from Earlier (phone keeps 'See all').

what: Pay's band is near-black green (sampled #112321 to #0E1C1B; rule is #17302D to #0C1918). Every other Employee and Lead screen uses the teal band (#0C726C to #08504C). It reads as a different product, or as dark mode on one tab.
why: DESIGN.MD: 'Band: one gradient'. One colour, one meaning (better-colors). The darker green was approved for the Owner's Payroll; the Employee page inherits it through the shared .c-pay class.
fix: Scope the dark band to Owner and Manager: add :not([data-employee-mobile]) to both rules so Employee Pay reads --b-band. If Jose wants Pay darker for everyone, record it in DESIGN.MD as the money band and use it on the Pay statement page too.

screens: Request time off 1440, Page not found 1440, all desktop pages
what: Two content widths with no visible logic: 1080px (Home, Schedule, Pay, Pick up and swap, Help, Add to calendar, More, the request form, 404) and 812px (Time off list, Notifications, Updates, Profile). The request form at 1080px has 516px date fields and a 1040px textarea (about 150 characters per line); the 404 card is 1080px wide holding 340px of content. The form's inset is 19px where every card uses 22–23px. 'Send request' is 40px tall.
why: Over-wide lines and fields (measure 60–75ch), dead area, and a form that looks stretched rather than designed. DESIGN.MD B6: reading pages are one 812px column.
fix: Forms and state cards join the 812px column; inside the form cap the field block at 560px (From and To 272px each with a 16px gap, textarea 560px). Card padding 22px. 'Send request' 48px, teal, right-aligned to the field block. 404 card max-width 560px.

what: Under 'Your week' sit two half-width cards: 'Coming up' (184px tall, two rows that repeat Wed and Thu from the grid directly above) and the open-shift card (66px tall). Bottom edges differ by 118px, leaving a hole under the right card.
why: Redundant content next to a ragged edge (TS-010 edit, don't list; shared edges).
fix: Right column becomes one card 'This week' the same height as the left: open shifts row, then 'What changed in your schedule' row (moved out of the week card's footer), each 64px with a chevron. Left card shows the selected day's detail (time, place, length, Shift details) instead of repeating two days; default selection is today.

what: In every day block the time breaks as '9:00 AM –' / '5:00 PM', leaving the dash hanging at the end of line one. Blocks are a fixed height, so five of seven are one-third empty (Employee) and Mon and Tue are half empty (Lead). In the Lead's today block the chips 'Starts in 8 h' and 'Shift lead' stack on two rows; other days have one.
why: A hanging dash is a wrapping defect (better-typography: wrap deliberately). DESIGN.MD B6 says chips sit in one row at the block's foot.
fix: Print the compact range on one line: '9 AM – 5 PM' at 14/20 700 tabular-nums, white-space: nowrap (compactRange already exists in home-b). Lines two and three stay. Chips in one row with a 4px gap; when two don't fit, the lead marker uses its short form 'Lead' (already in the markup for tablets). Block min-height 108px, chips pinned to the foot.

what: 'Shift lead · Customer Support · Main Office' does not fit 262px, so every upcoming row wraps to a third line holding only 'Main Office'. Rows grow from 64px (Employee) to 81px and the marker repeats five times in a row on Schedule.
why: Orphaned word on every row, inconsistent row height between roles, repetition instead of a summary. DESIGN.MD B6 already sets the pattern: say it once when a Lead leads the listed shifts.
fix: When every row in a card is a lead shift, drop the marker from the rows and show it once as the card's meta: 'You lead all 3' on Home's Coming up, 'You lead all 5' on Schedule's list (13.5/18 --b-grey, right of the title). Otherwise use the short marker 'Lead' in the sub-line on phones so the line stays one line.

what: Today's team adds a third button look to Home: a teal-50 tinted pill with teal text ('Write'), next to the grey 'Shift details' pill and the filled teal 'Review'. On desktop its note ('Your message goes to today's published team…') is 15px ink, while every other card note is 13.5px grey; the phone has no note.
why: Several button styles on one screen; the Lead addition has its own type and colour rules, so it reads bolted on.
fix: Make the row a plain navigating row (icon circle, title, sub 'Everyone on shift today · reading is optional', CaretRight) with no button; or use the same grey ghost as other row buttons (44px, 96px min). Note uses BCardNote (13.5/18 --b-grey) at both widths.

screens: Home, Help, More, Pick up and swap, Time off, Notifications, Updates; both widths
what: Row icons come in three treatments: teal glyph on teal-50 (Email support, Confirm rows, Today's team), dark-grey glyph on #F0F2F3 (most rows), amber glyph on amber tint (required notices). In Help's Contact card the first row is teal and every row below is grey. Add to calendar's accordion rows have no icon.
why: One weight and one treatment per context. DESIGN.MD B5: rows that lead with an icon draw it in a 36px teal-50 circle with an 18px bold glyph.
fix: Default every navigating row to the teal-50 circle with a teal 18px bold glyph. Reserve grey for facts that don't open (info, 'No open shifts'), amber for 'needs you', red for delete. Give Apple, Google and Outlook rows a calendar glyph circle.

screens: Home, Schedule, Pay, Time off, Availability, Pick up and swap
what: Explanatory notes live in four places: inside the card as its footer (Home, Time off, Pick up), on the canvas under the card (Schedule phone, Pay), in a ruled footer strip (Schedule desktop), and centred (Availability). The same fact is worded two ways: Home 'West Office hasn't published this week yet. Shifts shown are published.' and Schedule 'Your Main Office shifts are published. West Office hasn't published this week yet.' On Pay desktop the note starts at x=300, 4px in from the card edge and 19px left of the card text.
why: One voice, one vocabulary; shared edges. A note that moves from screen to screen stops being read.
fix: One rule: a note that qualifies a card is that card's footer (13.5/18 --b-grey, 22px inset, 12px above, 16px below, left-aligned, text-wrap: pretty). Canvas notes only when they qualify the whole page, aligned to the cards' text inset (22px). One sentence for the publication fact: 'West Office hasn't published this week yet.'

what: The icon sits in a 48px rounded square (about 12px corners), not the kit's circle, in red. Its inset is 17px where cards use 22px. 'Home' in the back link and 'Go to Home' in the card are the same action twice; the pill is the page's only teal element, 44px tall. On desktop the card is 1080px wide with 340px of content.
why: DESIGN.MD B2: one state card with a 48px icon circle; red means failed or stop, and a wrong link is neither. Looks like a default error box.
fix: Circle (999px), grey tone (#F0F2F3 fill, --b-ink2 glyph: MagnifyingGlass or Compass) via a 'missing' kind. Card padding 22px, max-width 560px. Keep the back link; make the action useful: 'Go to Home' teal 48px plus a ghost 'Open Schedule'. Title 16/22 600, line 14.5/20.

what: The Language switch is a rounded rectangle (about 10px corners, 34px thumbs, 40px track), while every other segmented control is a pill (44px track, 36px items). On the phone its hint is squeezed into a 150px column and wraps to three lines.
why: DESIGN.MD F5: one segmented control. Two shapes for one control on adjacent screens.
fix: Use the --b-seg-* tokens: 44px pill track with 4px padding, 36px pill items, 14/600. On phones stack: label and hint full width, control under them at full card width with equal columns.

what: On desktop the white 'Write an update' pill is the brightest element and 'Acknowledge' is a filled teal pill: two primaries, and the one a reader needs is the lower one. 'Open' and 'Acknowledge' stretch to 350px each. Body text starts at x=378, 1px off the title (377). On the phone 'Earlier' rows carry the word 'Unread' on its own third line plus a teal dot, and the title wraps.
why: One primary per view; buttons stretched to fill read as unfinished; state said twice.
fix: 'Write an update' becomes the glass pill at every width (it is a secondary action for an hourly employee). Desktop buttons hug their labels, right-aligned: ghost 'Open' (96px min) then teal 'Acknowledge', both 44px, 8px gap. Phone keeps two equal columns. Drop the visible word 'Unread' (keep it for screen readers); the dot plus a 600 title carries it.

what: Between the week strip and the shift list sit three separate one-row cards of different heights (84, 58, 86px), each with a different trailing element (teal pill, caret down, teal pill) and different left edges (text at x=81, x=32, x=81). The list the person came for starts at y=545, below the fold's midpoint.
why: Fragmented cards and competing actions push 'When do I work?' down; alignment drift (CR-402).
fix: One card 'This week' with three 64px rows sharing the 36px icon column: Confirm this week (teal pill), 2 open shifts (chevron), What changed (caret down, with a clock-counter-clockwise icon). 1px --b-line separators. This returns about 40px and puts 'Coming up' at about y=500.

what: 'Waiting' and 'Decided' have no counts (Pick up and swap's tabs do). Every row has the same grey sun icon and no state, so nothing says 'sent, waiting for your manager'. The helper line shares the card with the rows. The back link says 'Requests' while the Requests tab is already selected.
why: 'Did my request go through?' has no explicit answer; inconsistent tabs across sibling pages.
fix: Tabs: 'Waiting 3' and 'Decided' with the 20px count pill (F5). Each waiting row ends with an amber chip 'Waiting' before the chevron; decided rows end with green 'Approved' or grey 'Declined' (B5). Sub-line order: 'Thu · 1:00 PM – 5:00 PM' (drop 'Part of day' when a time range is shown).

what: Three equal columns hold labels of very different lengths. 'Open shifts 2' fills its thumb with about 5px of side padding (text starts x=29, thumb starts x=24); 'For you 1' has 20px each side.
why: Cramped label touching the thumb edge; uneven optical padding.
fix: At 360–430px size each item to its label plus an equal share of the remainder (the rule F5 already uses at 320–359px), minimum 12px side padding, 13.5px labels, 18px count pills. Or shorten the first label to 'Open'.

screens: Home 1440 (Employee), Help 1440, Pay 1440, Add to calendar 1440
what: Home's glass figure strip is 1080px wide with two cells whose content is about 100px each (80% empty glass). Help's Contact card ends at y=473 beside a right column that runs to y=715. Pay ends at y=520 with 380px of empty canvas. Add to calendar's two cards end at y=459 and y=449 (10px apart).
why: Over-airy regions and near-miss edges read as unplanned (CR-501 density; CR-402).
fix: Home: add a third figure for Employees ('Next shift · Today 9:00 AM', linking to the shift card) so the strip is three cells like the Lead's. Help: put Privacy and terms under Contact (left column) so both columns end within 24px. Add to calendar: align-items: stretch so both cards share a bottom edge. Pay: let 'Earlier' show up to five rows on desktop.

what: The workspace chip truncates its name: 'Northside QA Work…' (Employee) and 'Northside QA Wor…' (Lead, with 'Lead' under it). The Employee chip has no role line, so the nav sits 1px higher than the Lead's. Help's active state is a pill inset at x=28–204, while nav items highlight at x=16–216 with 8px corners.
why: Truncation with no way to the full value on the first thing in the rail; two active shapes in one sidebar.
fix: Let the name wrap to two lines (14/18 600, line-clamp 2) and add title/aria-label with the full name. Show the role line for both roles ('Employee', 'Lead') so the chip is one height (56px). Help's active state uses the nav items' box (x=16–216, 40px, 8px corners).
where: Shell sidebar (outside the files listed; corp shell / owner-b-shell.css). Not located precisely.

screens: Pick up and swap 1440, Lead Home 1440, Add to calendar 390, Help 1440
what: Last lines of one or two words: '…and you still meet / the rules.'; '…Shifts shown / are published.'; '…which can take / a while.'; 'Never email passwords, codes, bank details or / pay documents.' (the tile is 484px wide but the text breaks at about 310px).
why: Orphans (better-typography: text-wrap: pretty keeps a lone word off the last line).
fix: text-wrap: pretty on .b-cardnote, .b-note, .b-notice__s, .b-row__s and card body paragraphs; remove the max-width on Help's warning text.

what: 'Sign out' is a 58px white card with 22px corners and centred text, the same surface as the content cards, so it reads as an empty card. More's glass profile block has a white 'Profile and settings' pill on desktop and a full-width text row on the phone.
why: A control that looks like a container (keep controls distinct from content).
fix: Sign out as a ghost pill: 48px, #F0F2F3, ink 600, with a SignOut glyph, left-aligned under the cards on desktop (hugging its label) and full width on the phone.

what: The only colour on the page is the red 'Delete my account' row. 'Personal info' is three read-only values with no hint of who can change them. The page is called 'settings' and has one setting.
why: The eye lands on the one thing the person should rarely do; read-only values without a reason feel unfinished (B5: one read-only field shows a lock and the reason).
fix: Delete row: ink title 'Delete my account', grey sub 'Ends your access to this workspace', red-tinted icon circle only. Add a card note under Personal info: 'Your manager keeps these up to date.' Add Sign out as the first row of Account.

what: The Lead's desktop Profile has a 'Calendar and alerts' card (Add to calendar, Alerts on this device); the Employee's does not, although both roles use both features.
why: A Lead addition that isn't about leading; an Employee on desktop loses the shortcut.
fix: Show the card for both roles on desktop, or for neither.

what: Every day has the same small dot under its number, so the dots carry no information this week; past days (Mon, Tue) look the same as future days.
why: A mark that never varies is noise; past and future should differ at a glance.
fix: Past days at 60% white for the weekday and number; dot only on days with a shift (already the 'has' class) and a hollow ring for a day off. Keep today's white tile.

what: The footnote 'One-off days off go in Requests.' is centred; every other note in the app is left-aligned. The glass 'Change one week' pill is 36px tall (others in the band are 36–48px).
why: One odd alignment; mixed pill heights in the band.
fix: Left-align at the 18px inset; make 'Requests' a teal link to Time off. Band pills 44px on phones.

what: The update's body keeps the author's line break: '…back-office tablet.' ends a short line and 'Read it before your next close…' starts a new one with no paragraph gap, so it reads as a broken wrap.
why: Hard breaks inside a preview look like a rendering fault.
fix: In list previews collapse line breaks to spaces and clamp to three lines; show paragraphs (8px gap) only on the update's own page.

what: On pages taller than 900px the white sidebar stops at y=900 and the grey canvas continues under it to the page's end.
why: If real, the rail looks cut off when scrolled. It may only be how a full-page capture draws a sticky 100vh rail.
fix: Check in a browser at 1440×900 by scrolling to the bottom. If the rail ends, make it position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100dvh with the white fill on the grid column itself.
where: Shell sidebar CSS (outside the files listed)
